title: Backward variables and the diagonal identity
goal:
Implement the backward variables of Section 2.4 (Equation 18) and check the identity of Section 2.5 (Equation 19): summed along any anti-diagonal $t + u = n$ of the lattice, $\alpha(t, u)\,\beta(t, u)$ equals $\Pr(y \mid x)$.

`emit` has shape `(T, U)` and `null` has shape `(T, U+1)`, as in exercise 2. The starter already contains `forward`.

Write two functions:

- `backward(emit, null)` returns `beta` of shape `(T, U+1)`. `beta[t, u]` is $\beta(t+1, u)$ from Equation 18, with $\beta(T, U) = \varnothing(T, U)$.
- `diagonal_sums(alpha, beta)` returns an array of length `T + U`. Entry `n - 1` is $\sum_{t + u = n} \alpha(t, u)\,\beta(t, u)$ for $n = 1, \dots, T + U$, with the paper's 1-based $t \in 1..T$ and $u \in 0..U$. In 0-based array indexes, the node `[t0, u]` lies on diagonal `n = t0 + 1 + u`.
hints: Equation 18 in 0-based indexes: `beta[t, u] = beta[t+1, u] * null[t, u] + beta[t, u+1] * emit[t, u]`. Skip a term when its index runs past the lattice.
Fill from the far corner back: `t` from `T-1` down to 0, `u` from `U` down to 0. Set `beta[T-1, U] = null[T-1, U]` first.
A sanity check: `beta[0, 0]` is the probability of the whole sequence, so it must equal `Pr(y|x)` from `forward`.
`alpha * beta` is an element-wise product of two `(T, U+1)` arrays. Then add the entries `[t0, u]` whose `t0 + 1 + u == n`.
Allocate `np.zeros(T + U)`, then loop over every node and add `alpha[t0, u] * beta[t0, u]` into entry `t0 + u`. (That is `n - 1`, because `n = t0 + 1 + u`.)
